title: A Claude scope that cannot be named in a command still gets an unscoped update and an unscoped remedy (ruling 26 iii)
description: Introduced by QCLI-380 (#290, 5d408af) and pinned by its own test. When the deciding Claude row has a scope that is not a plain token, plainScope() drops --scope, so agents --update-instructions --target claude RUNS `claude plugin update opum-quest@opum` with no --scope, and the disabled remedy prints `claude plugin enable opum-quest@opum` unscoped. A command without --scope acts at Claude DEFAULT scope, which may be a different row from the one that decided the state. Ruling 26(iii) (opum-doc ADR Amendment 4) forbids this: an update names its deciding scope and never touches a row the reported state did not come from. MEASURED on origin/dev: test/qcli380-plugin-output-sanitised.test.ts "a scope that is not a plain token never reaches the update argv" asserts the calls [claude plugin list --json, claude plugin update opum-quest@opum], and it passes. lore-cli fixed the same defect in LCLI-593 (opum-ai/lore-cli#297, merged 46133fc0, review finding b). claudeScopeUnnamable(runtime, scope) is true for claude when the scope is not a plain token; the installed and disabled remedies become UNNAMABLE_SCOPE_REMEDY prose, and updateLorePlugin runs nothing and reports update not-run with updateDetail "the deciding scope could not be named in a command". Precedes, and is separate from, QCLI-382 (which tightens the token regex itself).

acceptanceCriteria.text: With a Claude deciding scope that is not a plain token, agents --update-instructions --target claude runs nothing beyond the list and reports update not-run, proven by a fake runtime that logs every call

The installed and disabled remedies for such a scope are prose naming claude plugin list --json and the row own --scope, never a runnable unscoped claude plugin command; the text matches lore-cli UNNAMABLE_SCOPE_REMEDY at 46133fc0 with the plugin id swapped
The QCLI-380 test that asserts an unscoped update runs is corrected; cited against lore-cli 46133fc0 and ruling 26(iii); bun run check exits 0

plan: 1. Add claudeScopeUnnamable(runtime, scope) and UNNAMABLE_SCOPE_REMEDY mirroring lore-cli 46133fc0 src/core/agent-plugins.ts:135-140; true for claude whenever the scope is not a plain token, absent included, as lore has it.

2. remedyFor returns that prose for installed and disabled when the scope is unnamable; updateQuestPlugin runs nothing past the list and reports update not-run with updateDetail "the deciding scope could not be named in a command".
3. Correct the two QCLI-380 tests that pin an unscoped enable remedy and an unscoped update argv; assert the fake runtime logged only the list.
4. bun run check; PR into dev.
implementationNotes: EVIDENCE. (AC1) test "a scope that is not a plain token never reaches the update argv" now asserts the fake runtime logged exactly ["claude plugin list --json"] and update not-run, updateDetail "the deciding scope could not be named in a command", no updateOk. (AC2) remedy for installed and disabled alike is unnamableScopeRemedy; a new test pins it byte-for-byte against lore-cli src/core/agent-plugins.ts:140 at 46133fc0 with LORE_PLUGIN_ID expanded, swapping opum-lore@opum for opum-quest@opum AND "so lore prints none" for "so quest prints none". The second swap goes beyond the AC wording ("with the plugin id swapped"): printing "lore prints none" from quest would be false, so the CLI self-name is swapped too. lore-cli is being told. (AC3) both QCLI-380 cases that pinned an unscoped enable remedy and an unscoped update are corrected and cite 46133fc0 and ruling 26(iii). MUTATION: pre-fix source with only the constant added turns exactly the predicted 3 of 14 red (the two corrected cases plus the new --check installed case). bun run check exits 0, 687 pass. SEMANTICS matched to lore: an ABSENT claude scope is also unnamable (lore isPlainScope(undefined) is false). Kept quest regex /^[A-Za-z0-9_-]+$/; the leading-character tightening is QCLI-382 F4.
finalSummary: A Claude deciding scope that is not a plain token (absent included) now gets no command at all: agents --update-instructions --target claude runs only the list and reports update not-run with updateDetail "the deciding scope could not be named in a command", and the installed and disabled remedies are prose (lore-cli UNNAMABLE_SCOPE_REMEDY at 46133fc0, plugin id and CLI name swapped). Why: ruling 26(iii); an unscoped claude plugin command acts at the default scope, which may be a different row. The QCLI-380 tests that pinned the unscoped behaviour are corrected. Verified by a logging fake runtime, a byte-parity test against the lore constant, a mutation run (3 of 14 predicted cases red on the pre-fix source), and bun run check exit 0.
